newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungaru's OTP to boost personal banking services.
newsitem.headline: Hungaru's OTP to boost personal banking services.

text.p: Hungary's largest commercial bank, OTP, said on Thursday it would introduce new products in an effort to strengthen its position in retail banking.
"As a part of its strategy, OTP would like to get nearer to individuals and households," deputy chief executive Adam Kolossvary told a news conference.
"There is sharp competition for the household market," he added. "It has very serious opportunities."
OTP, which is Hungary's market leader in personal banking, will make overdraft facilities available to individual current account holders from January 1, he added.
The maximum amount of the credit will be one million forints. The new product, called "A" credit aims at making the current accounts and the cards linked to them more attractive.
OTP declined to estimate how the "A" credit could change its position on the market, but added that it planned further developments to increase its role in personal finance.
OTP holds 1.5 million current accounts, with total deposits of over 182 billion forints.

However, the stock of retail loans dropped to 147 billion forints by the end of October from 175 billion forints at the end of last year due to the weakening of demand, a decline in home-building, and high interest rates in Hungary, the bank said.
OTP will also launch next week a new security, "Postajegy", to be sold in post offices to the bank's traditional clients who prefer simple products, the bank added.
